title: Understanding Sampling Distributions
text: Consider what happens when you take multiple samples from a population and calculate the mean of each sample.

title: Central Limit Theorem
text: The Central Limit Theorem states that the distribution of sample means will approximate a normal distribution as the sample size increases, regardless of the population's distribution.

hintAnswer: The distribution becomes more normal as the sample size increases.
title: Sample Size and Distribution
text: What effect does increasing the sample size have on the distribution of sample means?
choices: The distribution becomes more normal as the sample size increases.
The distribution becomes less normal as the sample size increases.
The distribution does not change with sample size.

title: Comparing Histograms
text: Think about how the histogram of sample means differs from a histogram of individual data points.

hintAnswer: A histogram of $$10000$$ sample means from samples of size $$n=1000$$.
title: Identifying the Normal Distribution
text: Which histogram would most closely resemble a normal distribution?
choices: A histogram of $$10000$$ sample means from samples of size $$n=1000$$.
A histogram of incomes from a SRS of $$n=10000$$ households.
A histogram of incomes from the entire census.
None of these would resemble a normal distribution.
